topic: Data type overflow and configuration access
summary_markdown:
The conversation covered technical issues related to data logging, specifically potential integer overflows for counters (like empty frames) and duration fields. It was determined that using `UInt64` for these parameters is necessary to prevent overflow when tracking long periods of inactivity or extended sessions.

Separately, the participants discussed accessing application configurations. [me] requested assistance in viewing/modifying app configs (e.g., `staging-mods`) within the staging environment, noting that the usual internal tool was inaccessible. A command using `helm get values` was provided to retrieve current configuration values.
decisions: Data logging counters and duration fields will be updated to use UInt64 data types to prevent overflow.
action_items: Someone needs to check the live data stream from the lidar source for new sessions/activity.
The configuration values for staging applications (e.g., `staging-mods`) can be retrieved using `helm get values staging-mops -n staging`.
